My yard is pretty small but my house is 3 stories and my pods are constantly up and down. My greyhounds prefer a more sedentary life.
They’re not busy like a border collie or a husky, they’re great family dogs. But they’re not going to sleep 18 hours a day like a greyhound would.

Depends on the type of pod you get. They’re jumpers and climbers and diggers. My big girl has to have a 6 foot fence. My little girl is more likely to go under the fence than over. Maybe you could add something to the top of your shorter sections to raise the height.

Here’s a nice article about Podencos:  medium.com/@saroltas/ad...
Many varieties - here are our 2. You’ll need a good fence. Senior Sighthound Sanctuary allows foster to adopt. Whichever group you use, fostering first is a good idea. They’re different dogs but great fun - very energetic.

Tahitian pearls are famous for their range: peacock, aubergine, silver-green. In a shot like this the colors answer each other.

We get these baroque South Sea pearls from the Timor Sea, between northwest Australia and Timor-Leste: remote, warm, and little known outside the pearl world. We're trained from 20th century marketing to expect perfectly round. These are ridged, no two alike. Oyster nacre follows its own logic.

Working the pearl farm at Ahe Atoll, French Polynesia. Those sleeves surround the oysters suspended in the lagoon. Along with indigenous fish that peck off the pests, these sleeves protect oysters from shell-boring parasites.

Ahe Atoll is at the northern edge of the Tuamotu Archipelago. There are 78 islands, most of them uninhabited. The water temperature here is 84°F year round. You need a 3-hour flight from Tahiti and a 30-minute boat ride. The Kamoka pearl farm has been operating here for 30 years.

With the right color compliment and contrasts even white pearls like these Japanese Akoya betray overtones of red, purple, and green. These are the same overtones that you see in the sky in southern Japan, subtly radiated by the Earth's only living gemstone.

Our design motif is the ecologically aware water droplet that becomes the outline of the chain link. The hang tag is in Australian mother of pearl, that smooth, iridescent substance that lines the inside of an oyster shell.
Just in time for Halloween: a really spooky combination of white wedding dress upset by black Tahitian pearls!

Beautiful, fanciful, ephemeral, the butterfly was regarded in ancient Egypt as a symbol of the soul's journey. Using Rhode Island metalsmith talent and tropical, mother of pearl for the irredescent wings, these jewels are worn as pins or brooches.
Here's an e-commerce close up of the Eddie Borgo TreasureLock design featured yesterday on model.
This is our TreasureLock design by Eddie Borgo. Each pearl (here a western Australian and a black Tahitian) has a shackle designed from two ecological droplets of water stretching to meet at the arc.

Three hearts lined up against a piece of quarry stone. There is mother of pearl from the white lipped oyster, mother of pearl from a black lipped oyster, and a lab-grown diamond made with wind power.  The middle chain is rose gold while the two on the outside are yellow gold.
These mixed color Tahitian black pearl strands go mostly from gray to green, but you see hints of purple and blue. The Pinctada margeritafera oyster, known as the black lipped oyster, produces them.

The dragonfly spends most of its life underwater as a nymph. It is a broad cultural symbol of transformation, change, the power of living in the moment. In Japanese culture the dragonfly (tombo) symbolizes courage, strength, and happiness.
The amazing color variation of Tahitian black pearls includes black, chocolate, copper, gray, green, blue, silver, purple, "aubergine", and "peacock".

Here's from our latest fashion shoot for the holiday season. The photographer is adjusting a beautiful mixed strand of Tahitian black pearls. We were blessed with a rental studio positioned to collect tons of natural light that you can see on the pink dress. This with my phone, no strobes.

These ocean pearls studs come from the west coast of Australia, an inaccessible place called Kuri Bay on the Timor Sea. Ocean pearls require pristine water to thrive - the remoteness from humanity makes a big environmental difference.

Like many things revolutionizing a world our grandparents wouldn't recognize, here are lab diamonds. This is crystallized carbon created in a laboratory with identical hardness, conductivity, optical properties as a diamond dug out of the ground. We like them for jewelry because we know the source.

Photo shoots are fascinating. So many visual and personality elements of the brand converge. We rented a studio on 8th avenue just uptown of Moynihan station in NYC. It was a fantastic day for natural light and that shaped everything we did and came away with.

A pearl farm image that captures the color, clarity, and richness of the pearl cultivation environment. Ocean oysters require a pristine environment to make pearls. This reality makes pearl farmers pragmatic environmentists who protect water quality to safeguard their livlihood.

This is the pearl farm at Kamoka on Ahe Atoll, French Polynesia. Josh Humbert's dad built it out on a coral knoll in the lagoon. It's near the equator so sunrise is pretty much the same time year round. And this is about the time they start each day.

The business of professional pearl farming and the flamboyant sport of undersea diving collide.  During the two years required for a grafted oyster to produce a pearl the shells must be cleaned about monthly to push back the shell-boring parasites that would damage the harvest or kill the oyster.

Pre-holiday season photo shoot yesterday in Manhattan with this lovely model, a woman almost irrationally beautiful. There were big, waist-to-ceiling windows in the studio we hired and so much beautiful autumn light that we hardly used the photo strobes at all. This shot was with my phone.

Bora Bora is an atoll with a mountainous island inset.  It's an incredible place with a name that sounds like a dream. The resorts are opulent while main town has a very local feel. There is a pronounced stray dog problem owing to resource allocation priorities. It is heartbreaking.

What a great shot from our colleagues at Kamoka Pearl in French Polynesia! That's their pearl farm where they work daily. It's a wooden platform built 100 ft out into the atoll lagoon on a coral head.  There's always time for a backflip! See the reef shark under him?

This bracelet strand of Japanese Akoya pearls is accented in a unique way: The pink gem is a ruby mined from Greenland. Rubies have an infamously conflicted sourcing history. Greenland offers a pure source alternative.
The inside of an oyster shell is coated with nacre. Layer on layer of the substance creates a smooth, optically iridescent surface. And that's what pearls are made of.

Ocean pearls are created over the course of a year or more, the oyster applying layer after layer of nacre, the same smooth, iridescent substance that lines the inside of an oyster shell. Truly, a pearl tells the story of the sea.
Lab-grown diamonds routinely come in big sizes, up to seven carats. The largest lab-grown diamond on record is a 150.42 carat.
We visit our Tahitian pearl farms, know our farmers by name, and can trace every pearl's journey from Atoll to your jewelry box.

What makes Tahitian pearls 'black'? It's layer after layer of dark nacre applied under the ocean waves from Pinctada margaritifera oysters. The layering creates iridescence: peacock greens, silver, and charcoal hues. Each pearl is as unique as a fingerprint.
These incredible cultivated pearls are from the west coast of Australia and come from the world's largest oyster, Pintada maxima, known as the white lipped oyster.

Good enough to eat? It takes 3 years for the Pinctada Margaritafera oyster to produce a black pearl after the oyster is grafted. The oyster is strung in the atoll lagoon in the vibrant waters a French Polynesia. The shells get cleaned from shell-boring parasites by the indigenous fish.

This is Kamoka Pearl Farm on Ahe Atoll (pop. 550). The farm is constructed of wood out on a coral head about 80 ft inside of the circular lagoon. In this relatively protected space the oysters are farmed, grafted for pearls, and harvested.

These luminous black pearls are from Fiji! We got the shipment before the August 7th tariffs. There's now reported delivery/shipment chaos in Fiji and we don't know when we can get more pearls.  Our red state friends insist that this disruption is due to "private equity".

This is Roseate Jewelry's design for a water-themed jeweled wand pendant. The design captures the fluid grace and serene power of life's most essential element, reminding us to connect with emotional depths, respecting our untapped powers.

As August turns to September the momentum builds toward the year's end, like the oyster's deliberate accretion of nacre, each conscious choice we make, in jewelry, in values, builds toward a luminous and lasting conclusion.

The Japanese word unami means a kind of mystic, untranslatable savoriness, the 5th element of flavors detectable in the mouth. This mixed strand of black Tahitian pearls suggests an almost unami quality with the delectable greens and purples on display.

This heart is designed from two ecological droplets of water joined. This heart is sublime because of the material, mother of pearl from the black-lipped oyster in Tahiti. It shows miraculous colors, changing in different light. Notice how it picks out the crimson from the flower behind it.

This heart-shaped lab diamond is structurally and optically identical to a mined stone. It is simply crystallized carbon created in a laboratory, this one from wind power. It has the same hardness factor as a mined stone - one of the big uses for these lab-grown diamonds is industrial.
Sunday morning sentiment: Preparing a fashion shot with mixed strand of Tahitian black pearls.

These 4-5 mm Japanese Akoya pearls have amazing luster and a tiny organic glow that shows the coloring of their tropical origin.  Modest pearl strands make for an incredibly subtle-yet-powerful fashion accent.
These black pearls come from the archipelagos of Tahiti. The color display is famed for the greens and purples. Mixed color Tahitian strands are our most popular item.

This strand of 5 - 6 mm Japanese Akoya pearls is fascinating for the vibrant colors that include silver, blue, peach and an abundance of springleaf green hues that jump out so nicely when pictured with green apples.

Summer is the perfect season for silver. In the waning days it's worth one more look. Silver metal prices are up this year, but nothing like gold! Gold is 75 times more expensive than silver by weight making silver jewelry a more approachable, affordable, casual choice.

Black pearls come from the Pinctada Margeritafera oyster in the islands and atolls of French Polynesia. Mixed strands of these oysters are our most popular. They have mysterious, compelling color shadings that dip into greens and purples.
These blue/green Akoya ocean pearls from Japan are born with amazing color tones that range from icy to spring leaf. Shot here with a pure white bloom.

It took Kokichi Mikimoto decades and near bankruptcy to first develop the method for grafting ocean oysters to produce cultured pearls. Eventually, he wowed Thomas Edison with his creation. 

This 3 mm white Japanese Akoya strand is part of that legacy.
This heart-shaped lab grown diamond is part of Roseate's TreasureLock collection. The shackle is designed from two ecological water droplets reaching together to form an arc.
Black pearls come from a Tahitian variant of the super large ocean oyster, Pinctada Margaritifera. The colors can go from black to grey, to purple, to green. This strand is rich with the green tones.

This heart is designed from two ecological water drops joined together. The material is mother of pearl from a Tahitian oyster. Mother of pearl is the inside layer of the oyster shell. You can see color variations when the light hits it. This is shot with my phone in our windowsill.

We did a photo shoot yesterday with a lot of on model shots to refresh our website offerings for the fall season. It's easy to get engrossed in the design and beauty of a created piece of jewelry and forget about the importance of scale and wearability, how that is visually communicated.

This is Josh and Celeste's pearl farm in French Polynesia where we source black Tahitian pearls. Three flights a week on Air Tahiti, rainwater collection and cisterns for drinking , compost toilets, lots of swarming sharks, and the most beautiful pearls on earth.

Beautiful golden pearls are primarily produced in the Sulu near the Philippines and Indonesia. They are not colored or dyed. The deeper the gold color the more valuable the pearl with the deepest called "24 karat" or "Imperial gold".
These heart-shaped diamonds from our TreasureLock collection are created in a lab, crystallized carbon that is optically and structurally identical to a mined diamond. And made with wind power.
What a perfect Saturday on Cape Cod!  Fete among the Flowers in Osterville hosted us for a pop-up event.
We make jewelry that has a simpler story. Diamonds from wind power. Pearls from small farms deep in the Pacific.  Simplicity Is the ultimate sophistication.

To all my streamer friends who need to hear this right now. You needn't switch from SAMMI. You can turn off updates and just rock it till the wheels fall off.

This change blindsided the lot of you and you're strapped for time and energy as is. Take as long as you need to adapt! We're here for you!
I had a sensation of blood in the water when all three current SAMMI devs step down, now I think I know why.

So regardless of my current feelings with Streamerbot, I don't think I'll be returning to SAMMI. I have too many friends affected by this directly and indirectly by the AI craze that this feels like the start of something bad.

ChatGPT, OpenAI, Google AI now summarizing our searches, Flock cameras, art generation, needless stuffing of it into every facet of our life cause some c-suite thinks buzzword popularity necessitates its use and wants to become some legendary forerunner. The list is EXHAUSTIVE and EXHAUSTING!
All the scientific and potential good case scenarios buried under just unadulterated greed. So is it any wonder its such a divisive topic when time and time again we've seen it used for ill?

Sadly, when there's speculation of profits or cost savings involved, humanity tends to lemming off a cliff for the side of ill intent. Too often I've seen it used as a shortcut, a sales marketing gimmick, a labor force reduction tool, or a magical problem solving elixir that's totally not a placebo.

Now here's where I get a little more charged. Yes, in the end of the day, AI is just a tool (please god let it not develop actual sentience while we're in our "grift towards Skynet" arc) but that means it can be used for good and also for bad.

Queue the Benny Hill theme as my tired ass reads through dozens of comments, visual examples, and a few documents that have shed a little more light on the recent stepping down of three other SAMMI devs and needless to say, I'm extremely disappointed.

What I was met with was a circus on fire. Chrizzz , the remaining developer for SAMMI down had decided to roll back changes concerning monopolies on extensions and the use of generative AI in the extension presentation.

Then everything changed when the Fire Nation attacked. Memes aside, I checked to see the notifications was pouring in from SAMMI discord. My friend Zoen said they finally released the fix for Twitch Combos and the bridge so I figured either something else broke or the fix backfired after deployment.

SAMMI's community felt more inclusive. Streamerbot lacked some things I liked from SAMMI plus some extension solutions. That and I've been stagnating on coding, with time being a limited resource, sometimes I just wanted a solution than to solve a problem. So I debated going back to SAMMI.
I figured that would help me dust off my programming roots and maybe code things that the tool didn't have a solution for without a full blown extension. Yet at times I've felt tempted to go back.

I've admittedly not been using SAMMI for some time despite how popular it has been in my friend and streamer circles. Not cause I dislike the product but because at times the code blocks felt a little rigid to use but also because Streamerbot offered a C# option for coding my own things.

TL/DR: Sticking to Streamerbot, not going back to SAMMI.

So had to wake up early today for a work meeting but then afterwards saw my discord notifications blow up, so instead of making the rational decision to catch up on sleep before catching up on the messages.

Boy I sure didn't need the stress after waking up early for a work meeting today. Sure, I could simply avoid posting about it but its probably not worth bringing some attention to. I've been on Streamerbot for some time but contemplated going back to SAMMI, though no longer.

And don't bother contacting Twitch about why you're not making revenue when you're supposed to be. They will simply give roundabout answers that will not give any solution to the problem. They give 0 care about why you're not making the revenue you're owed. Don't label your streams!

So if you want to make ad revenue, TURN OFF those labels! You're being screwed out of money! Following the rules is a detriment, and the revenue you're entitled to will be removed from you, without you knowing. Keep an eye on your revenue metrics, because this is the only way you'll know.

Thanks to a friend letting me know of this, I turned off those labels during the last stream, and MAGICALLY I started making ad revenue again. So what does this mean? Twitch is too concerned about their image to ad parties, that they won't play ads during your stream if you have labels on it.

Wanted to share this out - Proof that if you follow the rules as a streamer, you get screwed. For 2+ months I wasn't making ad revenue because I did as required, and put labels on my stream. Little did I know that it would cause Twitch to end my share of ad revenue.
